page.layout: One printed page, single text column with marginal notes in the left margin. Running head at top; page number 334 at top left. Notes in left margin: "Oftreæ quomodo ad comedendum præparandæ" (two lines, catchword-like marginal heading) and "NB." mark beside a paragraph.

main_text.p: falubrioris curiosi, nec non ventriculi imbecil-lioris, ostreas in ollis elixant, adiiciuntq; piper, cinnamomum & garyophyllos alii reclusas salis momento addito, prunis imponunt, parumq; concalefactas vorant. Galenus in farragine coqui a quibusdam docet. Alibi sale conditæ aut garo frguntur, quo cibo gentes quadam vtuntur frequenter. Ganeones ad Venerem stimulandam experimento iis vescuntur. Plinius lib. 32. cap. 6. stomachum unice reficere indistincte affirit, fastidiumq; mederi, alvumq; quoque leniter mollire, aitq; omnia testacea modice in cibis oportere collui, quia saporis gratia perit.

Celsus Cornelius lib. 2. eo capite, quo res stomacho idoneas explicat, pisces ex media materia ponit ostreas, pectines, cochleas. Idem tenerosque pisces & ostrea in his cibis numerat, quæ facile corrumpuntur, muricesq; & purpuras inter ea, quæ intus minus vitiantur. Præterea alvum moventibus contribuit ostrea, omnesq; ferè conchulas maxime ejus earum. Veteres in principio cœna ostreas præbere consueVisse. Plutarchus innuit 8. Symposi. 9. hodie mos invaluit apud quosdam extrinsecus, ostreas post alios cibos ingluttire, cum primis si præcesserint cibi duriores & astringentes, quæ difficulter corrumpuntur: cœstionem enim sic devorata impediunt, caloremque nativum ventriculi, cœstionem jam.

page.notes: Marginal text partly faint; the left-margin notes and the "NB." mark are transcribed as best possible. Several words in the margin and the Greek-derived names (Symposiacorum) are uncertain; the text is reproduced from the scan with doubtful letters not marked where legible.
